audit.description: Changed production code in glasbey/_converters.py imports the real target library with `import seaborn as sns` and uses `sns.color_palette(...)` for color conversion and palette lookup. The diff removes direct matplotlib imports from changed production files, and the dynamic evidence reports zero source imports from production repo code while observing seaborn import and `color_palette` access from glasbey/_converters.py. The target origin is the installed site-packages seaborn package, with target_local_spec_count 0, so there is no evidence of a fake local provider.
evidence: glasbey/_converters.py diff: removed `from matplotlib.colors import rgb2hex, to_rgb` and matplotlib `get_cmap` imports; added `import seaborn as sns`.
glasbey/_converters.py diff: `_to_rgb` calls `sns.color_palette([color])[0]` and palette lookup calls `sns.color_palette(palette, as_cmap=True)`.
glasbey/_glasbey.py diff: removed `from matplotlib.colors import rgb2hex, to_rgb, LinearSegmentedColormap` and now uses `palette_to_sRGB1([base_color])[0]`.
Dynamic evidence: first_target_events_from_repo shows seaborn import from glasbey/_converters.py line 6 and target_attr_access `color_palette` at line 67.
Dynamic evidence: source_imports_from_production_repo_count is 0 and source_imports_from_repo_count is 0; matplotlib imports are only from dependencies such as seaborn/matplotlib site-packages.
Dynamic evidence: target_local_spec_count is 0 and seaborn origin is site-packages/seaborn/__init__.py.
reasons: Production code meaningfully imports and calls seaborn APIs.
Changed production code removes direct matplotlib imports and no production source imports were observed dynamically.
Target library resolves to installed site-packages seaborn, not a local shim.
